pages.quiz:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #10
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Pronouns: Choose the correct sentence. (1 mark)
   A. The nurse helped me.
   B. The nurse helped my.
   C. The nurse helped I.
   D. The nurse helped mine.

2. Which word has the same first sound as 'tie'? (1 mark)
   A. van
   B. two
   C. fan
   D. die

3. Choose the correct -ing form of 'make'. (1 mark)
   A. makeing
   B. makking
   C. maiking
   D. making

4. Which word means 'to move from one person or place to another' (for example an illness)? (1 mark)
   A. diet
   B. signs
   C. spread
   D. cure

5. Which conjunction joins two negative ideas? (1 mark)
   A. and
   B. or
   C. nor
   D. so

6. Which list is in alphabetical order? (1 mark)
   A. aunt, brother, cousin, sister
   B. aunt, cousin, brother, sister
   C. sister, cousin, brother, aunt
   D. brother, aunt, cousin, sister

7. What is the plural of 'photo'? (1 mark)
   A. photees
   B. photoes
   C. photoss
   D. photos

8. Which sentence is a good ending for a story? (1 mark)
   A. Then a goat.
   B. And the sun.
   C. Farm.
   D. We caught the goat together, and I was tired but proud.

9. What is a password? (1 mark)
   A. A type of email
   B. A public name
   C. A secret word that only you know
   D. A friend's address

10. Why did Achieng tell Baraka to read his message before sending it? (1 mark)
   A. To make it longer
   B. To check the spelling
   C. To delete it
   D. To print it

11. In a comic, what do speech bubbles show? (1 mark)
   A. What the characters say
   B. The page number
   C. The price
   D. The author's name

12. Which word has a silent k? (1 mark)
   A. key
   B. king
   C. knee
   D. kind

13. A comic is a story told in (1 mark)
   A. a table
   B. a mathematical sum
   C. a series of small pictures
   D. a single long word

14. Which of these is a homophone pair? (1 mark)
   A. run and walk
   B. their and there
   C. hot and cold
   D. big and large

15. 'Who's' is a short form of which words? (1 mark)
   A. who was not
   B. whose is
   C. who is
   D. who has not

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Underline the prepositions: 'The children ran along the road, past the bank and into the market.' (3 marks)

17. Write a short dialogue of four lines in which you borrow a book from a friend politely. (4 marks)

18. Explain what it means to speak with expression. (2 marks)

19. Give two reasons why we must fill in forms carefully. (2 marks)

20. Explain two ways to make a story interesting. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #10 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — The nurse helped me.
   Me is the object form of I.

2. B — two
   Tie and two both begin with /t/. Die starts with /d/.

3. D — making
   Verbs ending in silent e drop the e before -ing.

4. C — spread
   Germs spread from person to person.

5. C — nor
   'Nor' follows a negative.

6. A — aunt, brother, cousin, sister
   a, b, c, s is the order of the first letters.

7. D — photos
   Photo just adds s.

8. D — We caught the goat together, and I was tired but proud.
   An ending tells how the story finishes and how people felt.

9. C — A secret word that only you know
   A password protects your account.

10. B — To check the spelling
   Checking finds mistakes.

11. A — What the characters say
   Speech bubbles hold spoken words.

12. C — knee
   In 'knee' the k is not pronounced.

13. C — a series of small pictures
   Comics use pictures, often with speech bubbles.

14. B — their and there
   They sound the same but are spelt differently.

15. C — who is
   Who's = who is (or who has).

SECTION B
----
16. (3 marks)
   Answer: along, past, into
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

17. (4 marks)
   Answer: A: Good morning, Ali. B: Good morning. A: May I borrow your book, please? B: Yes, here you are. A: Thank you.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for greeting, request, answer and thanks.

18. (2 marks)
   Answer: It means using the voice to show meaning and feeling by changing loudness, stress and pitch.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for using the voice and 1 for showing feeling or meaning.

19. (2 marks)
   Answer: The reader depends on the information, so a mistake may cause confusion or lost messages. Wrong information may delay help.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

20. (4 marks)
   Answer: Start with something that makes the reader curious, and add small details or similes. These help the reader picture the story and want to continue.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each way explained.
